newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Guangdong Power plans expansion.
newsitem.headline: China's Guangdong Power plans expansion.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd plans to start building a power plant with total investment of three billion yuan ($361.4 milion) in the first half of 1997, a company spokesman said on Friday.

The firm will have a 50 percent stake in the plant in the city of Zhanjiang in southwestern Guangdong province, the spokesman told Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin, adding the plant is scheduled for completion by 2000.

The other 50 percent stake in the plant, which will contain two generators with a capacity of 300,000 kW each, will be shared among three other domestic firms, the spokesman said. He did not identify the partners.

Construction of the plant will be divided into two phases, with the first phase to be finished in 1999, the official said, adding Guangdong Power will finance the first phase of construction with its own cash.
He said he expected an annual return of about 17 percent from the project upon operation.
The spokesman said Guangdong Power estimated higher net profit for 1996 against 1995 due to increased output of electricity and tax exemptions for 1996 and 1997. He did not give figures.
The company reported net profit, calculated under international accounting standards, of 376.97 million yuan for 1995.
"Electricity output rose on the operation of the company's 51-percent-owned power plant worth 2.4 billion yuan early in 1996," the official said.
The company has said it was granted the special tax treatment because it has been classified as a foreign-funded company following its offer of B shares to overseas investors.
It said the firm would pay an annual 7.5 percent corporate income tax from 1998 to 2000. Most China-listed firms are assessed at a 15 percent tax rate.

The power firm said that under international accounting standards, it notched up net profit of 296.1 million yuan in the first half of 1996, compared with 195.8 million yuan in the first half of 1995.
